literal: Migrating the Han River displaced persons to the banks at Mien. "Han River": all editions read "Han Prefecture"; at this time there was no "Han Prefecture"—changed according to Yuan Kuei 486.
idiomatic: Resettling Han River refugees on the Mien shore. "Han River": all editions read "Han Prefecture"; there was then no Han Prefecture—emended from Yuan Kuei 486.

literal: In the third month, ting-ssu. Below there is i-ch'ou.
idiomatic: Third month, ting-ssu. Below appears i-ch'ou.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-mao—there was neither ting-ssu nor i-ch'ou.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was ting-mao—neither ting-ssu nor i-ch'ou occurred.

literal: In the fourth month new moon was on ping-shen; the twenty-second day was ting-ssu; the thirtieth day was i-ch'ou.
idiomatic: The fourth month's new moon was ping-shen; the twenty-second day was ting-ssu; the thirtieth was i-ch'ou.

literal: The Comprehensive Mirror's collation variants say: "According to the long calendar, in the second month new moon was on jen-ch'en; the tenth day was hsin-ch'ou; the twentieth day was hsin-hai.
idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror's collation variants say: "According to the long calendar, the second month's new moon was jen-ch'en; the tenth day was hsin-ch'ou; the twentieth was hsin-hai.

literal: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was reduced in rank to General Who Garrisons the Army. "Chun": the Sung edition reads "hui."
idiomatic: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was demoted to General Who Garrisons the Army. "Chun": the Sung edition reads "hui."

literal: The Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Hall editions read "Tsan"; now corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Hsiao-wu.
idiomatic: The Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Hall editions read Tsan; corrected from the Annals of Emperor Hsiao-wu.

literal: The explanation appears in collation note thirty of this scroll.
idiomatic: See collation note thirty in this scroll.

literal: In the fifth month, on i-yu, the outlaw Ssu-ma Shun-tse styled himself King of Ch'i and seized Liang-chou city; on ting-ssu the Po-huang state; on wu-hsü the King of Ho-nan—all sent envoys presenting local products. According to the calendar, that year in the fifth month new moon was on chia-shen; the second day was i-yu; the fifteenth day was wu-hsü—there was no ting-ssu.
idiomatic: Fifth month, i-yu: the outlaw Ssu-ma Shun-tse declared himself King of Ch'i and held Liang-chou city; ting-ssu: the Po-huang state; wu-hsü: the King of Ho-nan—all sent tribute envoys. That year's fifth month had new moon on chia-shen; the second day was i-yu; the fifteenth wu-hsü—there was no ting-ssu.

literal: The ting-ssu entry is certainly in error.
idiomatic: The ting-ssu entry must be corrupt.

literal: Their livelihoods not yet established. "Established": all editions read "able"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 195.
idiomatic: "Their livelihoods not yet established." "Established": all editions read "able"; emended from Yuan Kuei 195.

literal: Wu-wu. All editions read "keng-wu"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: Wu-wu. All editions read keng-wu; emended from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on keng-hsu—there was no keng-wu.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was keng-hsu—there was no keng-wu.
